title: ClusterEA: Scalable Entity Alignment with Stochastic Training and Normalized Mini-batch Similarities

problem.claim: Entity alignment seeks to identify equivalent entities across different knowledge graphs, but embedding-based methods face geometric problems including hubness and isolation.

gap.claim: The increasing scale of knowledge graphs makes it difficult for entity-alignment models to apply normalization processes, limiting their use in real-world applications.

contributions.claim: ClusterEA is a framework for scaling entity-alignment models and applying normalization methods to mini-batches with a high entity-equivalent rate.
ClusterEA combines stochastic training, ClusterSampler, and SparseFusion to align entities between large-scale knowledge graphs.
The framework trains a large-scale Siamese GNN stochastically, samples highly overlapped mini-batches with ClusterSampler, and normalizes and fuses local and global similarities with SparseFusion.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe ClusterSampler as a novel sampling strategy for producing highly overlapped mini-batches.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on real-life datasets using entity-alignment benchmarks.
The authors report that ClusterEA can outperform the state-of-the-art scalable entity-alignment framework by up to 8 times in terms of Hits@1.

narrative_sequence.summary: Entity alignment identifies equivalent entities across knowledge graphs, and embedding-based methods dominate the task.
Embedding geometry creates hubness and isolation problems, while normalization becomes difficult to apply as knowledge graphs grow.
ClusterEA addresses scalability through stochastic training, ClusterSampler, and SparseFusion.
Experiments on real-life benchmark datasets are reported to show improvements over a state-of-the-art scalable framework.

source_observation.claim: The framework applies normalization to highly overlapped mini-batches and fuses local and global similarity information.

interpretation.claim: Mini-batch construction and multi-scale similarity handling may help adapt normalization to large-scale entity-alignment settings.

application.claim: For large-scale alignment tasks, consider sampling mini-batches with high entity overlap and combining local and global similarity signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the reported entity-alignment benchmarks or other graph settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark dataset names, sizes, or data splits.
